newsitem.title: USA: GTE offers new overseas long-distance plan.
newsitem.headline: GTE offers new overseas long-distance plan.

text.p: GTE Corp said it introduced an international calling plan for residential customers that offers prices competitive with other major U.S. carriers on direct-dialed calls to most countries overseas.

GTE also said it had signed up the millionth customer for its long-distance service, which it introduced only one year ago. GTE was the first major U.S. provider of local phone services to enter the long distance business.
The company said pricing is determined by the time of day a call is placed from within the United States, with peak- and off-peak period rates. The plan covers calls to 232 countries.
The plan has no enrollment fee and carries a $3 monthly charge. GTE also offers flat-rate plans for domestic calling.
GTE's international calling plan is available to U.S. customers immediately, according to Rob McCoy, president of GTE's Long Distance division.
In a few weeks, McCoy said the company plans to begin rolling out a similar service to overseas callers targeted at specific interest groups or on a country-by-country basis.
GTE said it is waiving calling periods for calls to Asia, Africa and Europe, applying one rate for each country -- no matter what time of day or night the call is placed.

"Many calling plans are based on the time of day in the country called," McCoy said. "The beauty of this plan," he said, "is that consumers can stop worrying about placing calls during high-cost times."

For example, GTE said U.S. callers dialing to Japan would pay $0.47 per minute for a morning call, which compares to AT&T's rate of $0.47, MCI's rate of $0.48 per minute and Sprint's $1.40 per minute rate.
Calls to Mexico City and Jamaica were cheaper than its rivals at certain calling times, according to a GTE statement.
However, the cost of a call to the United Kingdom will be $0.35 per minute compared to the $0.12 per minute charged by AT&T and MCI currently. Sprint also charges $0.35 per minute.
The $0.12 per minute rate means AT&T and MCI are currently charging cheaper rates for calls to Britain than they charge for U.S. domestic long-distance calls, McCoy suggested.

However, he cautioned that GTE would avoid competing with rivals solely on price. "I will not compete with suppliers who are clearly pricing well out of market range for what I suspect would be a limited period of time," he said.
"It's not sustainable," he said.
"I can guarantee that in the vast majority of countries we are going to be right there with MCI, Sprint and AT&T," McCoy told Reuters in a phone interview.
He also said GTE was "on track" to make its long distance business profitable by the fourth quarter of 1998.

GTE sees long-distance as a means of boosting the "wallet share" of its existing customers' communications bill, building on the relationships built with its established base of residential and business local and wireless services.
The company reported $50 to $60 million in long distance in revenues during 1996, and has told analysts it expects to increase that figure by seven-fold in 1997, McCoy said.
GTE stock closed down 7/8 at 46-3/4 Wednesday.
((-- E. Auchard, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1736))
